title: Compact bridges for incremental tool events: TS/Py/Go SDK samples & compatibility plan
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: design and ship small, language-idiomatic bridge helpers for incremental tool/function events and structured outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. These helpers should: (1) provide a minimal framing/envelope for partial tool outputs (fragments), (2) include an idempotency + resume protocol for intermittent connections, (3) expose ergonomic listener/iterator APIs per-language, and (4) offer a compatibility shim layer to make older SDK clients work with new framed events. Motivation: customers are building tool-driven flows (tool calls, function outputs, structured JSON emission) that arrive incrementally; current SDK patterns are ad-hoc across languages which increases bugs and support load. This ticket defines the protocol and provides reference implementations and examples for the SDKs so downstream teams can adopt a single interoperable pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc describing message envelope, sequence semantics, resume token format, and merge semantics is published to Confluence (link in comments).
TS/Python/Go reference helpers implemented in SDK repos with unit tests exercising fragmentation, out-of-order fragments, and resume behavior.
Migration guides (one-pager) available for existing streaming clients to opt into framed events with backward compatibility toggles.
A minimal integration example app demonstrates tool calls where structured JSON is emitted across multiple fragments and final output is reconstituted correctly.
Performance: per-message framing adds <2% CPU overhead on typical small-fragment workloads (bench numbers in comments).
design_decisions: Use a compact JSON envelope rather than binary protobuf to keep compatibility with browser clients and basic REST transports.

Envelope fields: {t: 'fragment'|'meta'|'end', s: seq_number, r: resume_token (optional), id: invocation_id, p: path (optional), b: base64(payload) } — chosen to reduce field name size across the wire.
Fragments are ordered by seq_number; SDKs will accept out-of-order fragments but will buffer until missing seqs exceed a configurable threshold, then switch to 'best-effort' merge mode.

Resume token is an opaque base64 string generated by the server containing last-seen-seq and a short HMAC; clients can present it to resume from that point. Tokens are short-lived (default 5 minutes).

Compatibility shim: servers will continue to send legacy newline-delimited text events for clients that opt-out; new framed mode is opt-in via header 'X-RI-Framed: 1'. SDK helpers will auto-detect framed vs legacy streams.
Backpressure: TS/Go helpers expose manual pause/resume hooks; Python async iterator respects awaitable backpressure points. This prioritizes developer ergonomics over transparent automatic batching.
Security: payloads may contain sensitive structured outputs; SDKs will expose an opt-in 'redaction' callback to mask tokens before logging in dev builds.
integration_examples:
Python (async generator) reference:

# Minimal iterator to reassemble fragments from a framed text stream
from typing import AsyncIterator
import asyncio, json, base64
async def consume_framed_stream(ait: AsyncIterator[str]):
    buffers = {}
    async for line in ait:
        env = json.loads(line)
        id = env['id']
        buffers.setdefault(id, {})[env['s']] = env.get('b', '')
        if env['t'] == 'end':
            parts = [buffers[id].get(i, '') for i in sorted(buffers[id].keys())]
            payload = json.loads(base64.b64decode(''.join(parts)).decode())
            yield {'id': id, 'payload': payload}
            del buffers[id]

# In aiohttp you can wrap resp.content.__aiter__ to feed into consume_framed_stream

Notes: these are intentionally minimal reference patterns; production SDKs will add buffering thresholds, resume-token exchange helpers, hooks for redaction and logging, and optional binary framing optimizations for internal runtimes.
rollout_plan: Publish Confluence protocol doc and RFC for internal review (Week 0).
Merge reference implementations into sdk-js, sdk-py, sdk-go repos behind feature flag 'framed-events'.
Create a migration guide and example app repo (tool-demo-fragments) demonstrating server->client framed stream and fallback to legacy streams.
Run canary with internal customers (2 teams) for 2 weeks, collect perf/bug telemetry, then toggle default on for new tokens.
Formalize API in public SDKs and include examples in 'getting-started' quickstarts for each language.
test_plan: Unit tests: fragment reassembly, out-of-order arrival, duplicate fragments, missing fragment timeouts, resume with valid/invalid tokens.
Integration tests: end-to-end demo app using local server that emits fragments; run under CI for all SDKs.
Load tests: simulate 10k concurrent small-fragment streams to measure CPU/mem and ensure <2% overhead introduced by framing logic.
Security tests: ensure resume token expiry and HMAC verification, verify redaction callback paths do not leak secrets into logs.
